title: Factoring
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
simplifyHint: Close: that's a common factor, but not the greatest one. There's still a common factor inside the parentheses.

hints.poly.factor.gcf: Find the biggest number that divides every term. Write it outside, and divide each term by it inside.
hints.poly.factor.trinomial: Find two numbers that multiply to the last number and add to the middle number. Check by multiplying back.
hints.poly.factor.diff-squares: A square minus a square: (first + last)(first − last). x² − 25 = (x + 5)(x − 5).
hints.poly.factor.leading: Multiply the first and last numbers. Find two numbers that multiply to that and add to the middle. Split the middle term and group.
hints.poly.factor: GCF first. Then: two numbers that multiply to c and add to b; a square minus a square; or split the middle (ac method).

misconceptionMessages.poly.gcf-one-term: Divide EVERY term by the common factor: 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3), since 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
misconceptionMessages.poly.factor-signs: Check the signs by multiplying back: the middle term should come out with the sign it has.
misconceptionMessages.poly.factor-sum: Those numbers multiply to the right number, but check that they also ADD to the middle number.
misconceptionMessages.poly.diff-squares-same-sign: One factor needs + and the other −, so the middle terms cancel: (x + 5)(x − 5) = x² − 25.
misconceptionMessages.poly.factor-placement: Right numbers, wrong places: multiply back and the middle term comes out wrong. Try swapping the last numbers.

sections.title: Greatest common factor
sections.objective: Factor out the greatest common factor: 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
explain: Factoring undoes multiplying: 3(2x + 3) multiplies out to 6x + 9.
Use the GREATEST common factor, so nothing more comes out of the parentheses.
sections.key: Find the biggest number that divides every term. Put it outside; divide each term by it inside. Check by multiplying back.

sections.title: Factor x² + bx + c
explain: Multiplying (x + 3)(x + 4) gives x² + 7x + 12: the numbers multiply to 12 and add to 7.

visual.caption: Multiplying (x + 3)(x + 4). Factoring x² + 7x + 12 is this in reverse.

sections.key: Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. Then x² + bx + c = (x + one)(x + other).

sections.title: Difference of squares
explain: x² − 25 has no middle term. That happens when the two factors are the same except for the sign: the x terms cancel.
sections.key: A square minus a square: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). x² − 25 = (x + 5)(x − 5).

sections.title: Factor ax² + bx + c
explain: When there's a number in front of x², multiply it by the last number first.
Then split the middle term into two pieces and factor in pairs.
sections.key: Multiply a × c. Find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b. Split the middle term, group in pairs, and factor each pair.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: GCF first. Then: x² + bx + c (multiply to c, add to b), a square minus a square, or the ac method.
